title: Circuit breaker, retry with backoff, and the retry storm

videos.script: Lesson 5 ended with a timeout, which turns a slow failure into a fast one. This lesson is about what to do next. {{next}} The obvious answer is to try again. Most failures between services are brief, and a second attempt a moment later often works. {{retry}} On your machine you will see a retry turn a service that fails one call in five into one that almost never does. {{works}} Then you will freeze that service for three seconds, the length of a long garbage-collection pause, with the checkout calling it sixty times a second. {{freeze}} Without retries it recovers on its own. With three retries it never does, for as long as the checkout keeps calling. The retries are the outage. {{storm}} You will try the standard fixes in turn: waiting before each retry, with randomness, and then a circuit breaker, which stops calling a service that is clearly not answering. {{breaker}} Only one of them brings the service back, and the numbers show why.
